exposure: mode of delivery (cesarean section vs. vaginal delivery)
cohort: The study included children born in Taiwan between 2004 and 2013 whose maternal and child health data were linked from the National Health Insurance Research Database (NHIRD).
finding: Cesarean section significantly increased the risk of childhood asthma, allergy rhinitis, atopic dermatitis, respiratory tract infection, and overweight, even after adjusting for confounding factors.
mod_finding: Children delivered by cesarean section more commonly developed respiratory tract infections, asthma, allergic rhinitis, atopic dermatitis, and obesity than children delivered vaginally.
